# Chapter 4 · Markup.escape and the Reassembled Page > **Enters as:** `s = Markup('Alice "The <b>Great</b>"')`, arriving at `Markup.escape` from the last line of `format_field` The anchor has come back out of `User.__html_format__` and is now the local `rv` inside `EscapeFormatter.format_field`. The method has one line left: `return str(self.escape(rv))` ([`__init__.py#L354`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L354)). Every branch of the dispatch — the `__html_format__` door, the `__html__` door, the default door — funnels through this same escape call. That is the point of the design: there is one exit, and nothing leaves a format field without passing it. So the anchor, tags and all, is handed to the escaper. ## A second trip that changes nothing `self.escape` is `Markup.escape`, the classmethod ([`__init__.py#L230-L240`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L230-L240)). It calls the module-level `escape` and inspects what comes back. Inside `escape`, the anchor fails the exact-type test — `type(s) is str` is false for a `Markup`, which is a *subclass* of `str` ([`__init__.py#L39`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L39)) — and falls to the `__html__` branch ([`__init__.py#L42-L43`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L42-L43)). `Markup.__html__` returns `self` ([`__init__.py#L133-L134`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L133-L134)), and the result is passed to `Markup(...)`, whose constructor checks for `__html__` once more and calls it a second time ([`__init__.py#L125-L126`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L125-L126)) — the trace shows both calls, at depth and again one level in. For a `Markup` that is cheap. For a user-written `__html__` that queries a database or builds a fragment, it is two invocations per `escape` call; worth knowing if yours has a cost or a side effect. What `Markup(...)` produces here is a *fresh* `Markup` carrying the same characters — `str.__new__` on a subclass always allocates ([`__init__.py#L128-L129`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L128-L129)); no replacement ran, so the text is identical. Back in `Markup.escape`, that value's class is compared with `cls`: `rv.__class__ is not cls` is false, so `escape`'s result is returned as-is instead of being pushed through `cls(...)` a second time ([`__init__.py#L237-L240`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L237-L240)) — one wrap saved on a path that runs once per format field. That comparison is also what makes `Markup` subclassable: if an application defines `class MyMarkup(Markup)`, `MyMarkup.escape(x)` *does* re-wrap the plain `Markup` that `escape` produced, so the subclass survives escaping, formatting, joining and concatenation. The anchor therefore reaches `str(...)` with its text unchanged, and `format_field` returns the bare string `'Alice "The <b>Great</b>"'`. The tags are alive. The name inside them is still escaped, exactly once. > **For the owner:** This is the trust boundary in its most concrete form. The anchor was built by MarkupSafe's own formatter, so its tags are there by construction — but `escape` cannot tell that apart from an `__html__` that pasted raw request data between two angle brackets. Whatever an `__html__`/`__html_format__` returns as `Markup` is inserted verbatim, here and anywhere else. When reviewing, the question is not "does the template escape?" (it does) but "does every `__html__` in our codebase build its output through `Markup(...).format` or `escape`, rather than f-strings over user data?" One careless `__html__` defeats everything downstream of it. The mirror image is a quieter surprise in your favour: if `__html_format__` returns a *plain* `str` containing tags, this line escapes it and the tags show up as visible text rather than markup ([`docs/formatting.rst#L17-L19`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/docs/formatting.rst#L17-L19)). ## The second field, and the join `vformat` moves on to `{comment}`. The trace elides it — `EscapeFormatter.format_field ×1 more` — because it is the path just walked. The value is `Markup('<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>')`, the escaped comment from chapter 1. Being a `Markup`, it takes the first door, `__html_format__`, which returns `self` for an empty spec ([`__init__.py#L325-L329`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L325-L329)), and then the same `escape` round trip leaves its text untouched. Its `<script>` is not escaped into `<script>`; the comment is rendered once and only once, no matter how many `Markup` layers it passes through. `string.Formatter.vformat` now concatenates the trusted literal pieces of the template — `'

User: '`, `' said: '`, `'

'` — with those two plain strings, and `Markup.format` wraps the whole joined result in `self.__class__(...)` ([`__init__.py#L313-L315`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L313-L315)). The trace records that final constructor call with the complete page text. This single wrap is where the safe type is restored, after the standard library has done its plain-string work; the bare `str`s in between were never visible outside the formatter. The page leaves as `Markup('

User: Alice "The <b>Great</b>" said: <script>alert(document.cookie);</script>

')`, and `print(repr(page))` sends it through `Markup.__repr__` ([`__init__.py#L167-L168`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L167-L168)), which prefixes the class name so a safe value is distinguishable from a plain string in a log or a REPL. The scenario's `assert "") assert safe_comment == Markup("<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>") user = User(3, 'Alice "The Great"') anchor = user.__html_format__("link") ANCHOR = ( '' "Alice "The <b>Great</b>"" "" ) assert anchor == ANCHOR assert type(anchor) is Markup # --- trace 45-54: Markup.escape(anchor) -> escape -> __html__ -> same text assert anchor.__html__() is anchor # __init__.py:133-134 escaped_anchor = Markup.escape(anchor) assert escaped_anchor == ANCHOR # unchanged: tags survive, name stays escaped assert type(escaped_anchor) is Markup # Markup(...) on a subclass always allocates, so this is a fresh equal object assert escaped_anchor is not anchor # the re-wrap branch: a Markup subclass gets its own type back (L237-238) class MyMarkup(Markup): pass sub = MyMarkup.escape(anchor) assert type(sub) is MyMarkup assert sub == ANCHOR # and plain Markup.escape did NOT return a subclass-wrapped value assert type(Markup.escape(sub)) is MyMarkup # rv.__class__ is MyMarkup, cls is Markup # --- trace 55: format_field hands vformat a *plain* str ------------------- formatter = EscapeFormatter(Markup.escape) rv_user = formatter.format_field(user, "link") assert type(rv_user) is str assert rv_user == ANCHOR # --- trace 56: the {comment} field, same path, also unchanged ------------- rv_comment = formatter.format_field(safe_comment, "") assert type(rv_comment) is str assert rv_comment == "<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>" # --- trace 57-59: vformat joins, Markup.format wraps the result ----------- template = Markup("

User: {user:link} said: {comment}

") page = template.format(user=user, comment=safe_comment) EXPECTED = ( '

User: ' "Alice "The <b>Great</b>"" " said: <script>alert(document.cookie);</script>

" ) assert page == EXPECTED assert type(page) is Markup # the wrap at __init__.py:315 restored the type assert "
